tone_statements.citation: Rasmussen, Kent. 2018. A Comparative Tone Analysis of Several Bantu D30 Languages (DR Congo). PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. xxviii+279 pp. (Linguistics & TESOL Dissertations 116, UTA MavMatrix; Glottolog ref 589182.)
tone_statements.quote: These languages make use of contrastive pitch (tone), which is a source of difficulty in their analysis. ... The Bantu D30 languages have similar consonant and vowel inventories, and similar numbers of lexically contrastive tones. ... Tonally, Ndaka, Mbo, and Budu have the same system, which opposes 1s and 2s against all other forms, in a simple binary split between simple speech act participants versus others. ... past and future TAM is distinguished only by tone, as is the case for all the Bantu D30 languages.
tone_statements.locator: Appendix C 'Orthographies of Bantu D30 and the functional load of tone', pp. 242 and 244 (Budu paradigms exx. 58-59 on p. 245; Table 70 on p. 249)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone (H vs L root classes + depressor-conditioned rising/lowered patterns; consonant-tone interaction) plus grammatical tone (past/future distinguished only by tone); inventory not stated numerically for Budu (a work listed here give H, L + rising after depressors).

sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Budu' (bdu), source Asangama 1983 (local CLDF copy
sources.note: No stress features (14A-17A) coded for Budu; only morphosyntactic features.

sources.citation: Kutsch Lojenga, Constance. 1994. KiBudu: a Bantu language with nine vowels. Africana Linguistica 11: 127-133. doi:10.3406/aflin.1994.948
sources.note: Nothing. p.128 gives consonant and nine-vowel inventories and tone marking (H, L, LH rising; fn.2: rising tone correlates with depressor consonants); body is ATR vowel harmony (Ibambi dialect). No mention of stress or accent. (Persee per-page scanned text. the PDF itself is captcha-gated.)

sources.citation: Frieke-Kappers, Claertje. 2007. The Creative Use of Genre Features: Continuity and Change in Patterns of Language Use in Budu, a Bantu Language of Congo (Kinshasa). PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (hdl 1871/11028), 467 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.3 linguistic sketch and Appendix 3.A (pp.136-138 = printed 119-121) treat vowels/ATR harmony, consonants and tone only: 'Budu has High (H) and Low (L) tone. H is realised as rising surface tone (R) if it follows a depressor consonant' (p.121); p.67 'Budu has a tonemic Rising tone (R)'. Explicitly defers tone rules and phonology to Asangama 1983 and Kutsch Lojenga 1994. Full-text search for stress/accent/penultimate/prominence finds no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Bokula, Francois-Xavier. 1970. La langue bodo: formes nominales. Africana Linguistica 4: 63-84. doi:10.3406/aflin.1970.878
sources.note: Nothing. 'Apercu phonologique' pp.67-71; 'B. Les phonemes supra-segmentaires' (p.71) lists only 1. quantite vocalique and 2. tonalite ('deux tonemes essentiels: le toneme haut.. le toneme bas'); p.73 morphotonology. Northern (Wamba) dialect. No accent/stress paragraph.
